short: Hadrian's rebuilding, completed around 128 CE, produced the largest unreinforced concrete dome ever built.
full:
The Pantheon standing today is Hadrian's rebuilding, raised between roughly 118 and 128 CE on the site of an earlier temple built by Agrippa in the 20s BCE and twice destroyed by fire. Hadrian kept Agrippa's original dedicatory inscription on the new porch, which misled scholars for centuries into dating the whole building to Augustus's reign until brick stamps confirmed its true, Hadrianic date. Behind a conventional colonnaded porch, the building opens into a rotunda roofed by a coffered concrete dome 43 metres in diameter, its weight graduated by using progressively lighter aggregate toward the crown and lit only by a single unglazed oculus.

The dome's span was not exceeded by any structure for over a millennium. Converted into a church dedicated to Saint Mary and the Martyrs in 609, the building owes its unusually complete survival to that continuous religious use, unlike almost every other major structure of pagan Rome. Its proportions, in which the interior height equals the dome's diameter, and its coffering pattern became reference points for architects from the Renaissance onward, studied and copied by Brunelleschi, Michelangelo and countless others.
